chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar said:
I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who speaks in the obligatory prayer about anything, conversing with his Lord. He said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak during the obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the permissibility of speaking during the obligatory prayer (Salat al-Farid) for those who are not reciting the Quran or performing Ruku/Sujud, allowing them to converse with their Lord about any matter. This ruling highlights the distinction between the mandatory recitations and the optional nature of other speech, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that such speech does not invalidate the prayer provided it is not excessive or distracting. It underscores the concept of *khushu* (devotion) as an internal state rather than strict silence, permitting personal supplication or conversation within the prayer structure.
